components.description: University Policy 05-035 (effective 2017-09-01): 60 hours of paid parental leave at 100% of regular pay for an eligible faculty member (0.50 FTE or more, 180 days of service) upon the birth or adoption of a child, used within 18 weeks of the birth or adoption; one benefit per employee per birth or adoption event.
components.faculty_group_note: "An unclassified academic or professional faculty member" with "an appointment of 0.50 FTE or greater"; policy title "Paid Parental Leave for Faculty"
components.eligible_parent_wording: birth mother, biological father, spouse, domestic partner, or adoptive parent
components.service_requirement: employed for at least 180 days; appointment of 0.50 FTE or greater
components.dual_employee_rule: each may take: both are entitled and may take the leave concurrently or at separate times
components.duration_note: 60 hours at 1.0 FTE (= 1.5 weeks, R11). Proportional for 0.50 to <1.0 FTE; 'Eligible employees on an academic year appointment will receive a pro-rated amount of paid parental leave for any portion of the sixty (60) hours (1.0 FTE) that occurs in the academic year' (5.2.3); pro-rated where eligibility is attained during the leave (5.2.4). Continuous or intermittent use (5.3.2); unused hours forfeited after 18 weeks (5.3.3). 'The first year implementation is effective September 1, 2017 and will provide sixty (60) hours'. May also be used in cases of stillbirth (5.3.4). May supplement a short-term disability benefit to make up to 100% of salary (5.4.2); the short-term disability plan itself is not described in any saved source.
components.pay_fraction: 100% of the employee’s regular rate of pay
components.relief_note: Paid time off; no relief terms stated (R9).
components.time_window: must be used within the eighteen (18) weeks immediately following the birth or adoption
components.return_obligation: reimburse the paid parental leave benefit if the employee fails to return after the leave, or returns but fails to remain actively at work for at least thirty (30) calendar days; not required where failure is due to a serious health condition of the employee or child or other circumstance beyond the employee's control

Governing document for faculty parental leave: University Policy 05-035 Paid Parental Leave for Faculty (effective 2017-09-01, in force on the reference date): 60 hours at 100% pay at 1.0 FTE (1.5 weeks). The Leave Administration manual (revised March 2008) describes itself as 'a general information publication only' and defers to rules and statutes; it is linked as current from Policy 05-035 (8.1) and is used for the sick-leave, advance and classified provisions.

Birth parent chain: OFLA pregnancy-disability leave 12 weeks (c7), with the 60-hour paid parental leave (c1) and FMLA 12 weeks (c5) starting with it -> OFLA parental leave 12 weeks (c6) -> OFLA sick-child leave up to 12 weeks only if the child needs home care (c8). Own sick leave (c2, own balance) and the sick-leave advance (c3) may pay part of the absence; sick leave without pay up to one year (c4, discretionary) follows exhausted sick leave.
Non-birth parent chain: 60-hour paid parental leave (c1) with OFLA parental leave 12 weeks (c6) and FMLA 12 weeks (c5) starting together -> OFLA sick-child leave up to 12 weeks (c8, conditional).

S1a judgment: ORS 659A.162(3)(a) states pregnancy-disability leave is 'In addition to the 12 weeks of family leave', so OFLA parental leave (c6) is linked consecutive_after c7 for the birth parent (roles: birth) and concurrent_with c1 for the non-birth parent (roles: nonbirth). The documents rely on OFLA for pregnancy ('leave is needed for a serious health condition, pregnancy, parental, bereavement...') and link 'Pregnancy Disability Examples'.

Not coded: Policy 05-035 5.1.6-5.1.7 ask departments to be flexible and to manage workload; no relief or benefit is granted. Health insurance continues during FMLA/OFLA leave (employer share of premiums) — not leave, pay or protection of its own. Short-term disability is named in 05-035 5.4.2 but no saved source states its terms (flag on c1).
